key_insight: Realistic piezoelectric surface deformations can reshape near-wall turbulence and produce meaningful drag reduction, with spanwise waves performing best.
engineering_relevance: This suggests an actionable path to active flow control using hardware-compatible wall actuation for reducing skin-friction drag in channels and similar wall-bounded flows.
method: Performed DNS of turbulent half-channel flow at Re_tau=200 over actuated wall deformations.
Modeled piezoelectric actuation with FEA across practical frequency and voltage ranges beneath an aluminum sheet.
Imposed the resulting wall deformations as boundary conditions to test upstream, downstream, and spanwise wave effects on drag.
evidence_signal: The study reports maximum drag reductions of 1.6% for upstream, 5.4% for downstream, and 27.6% for spanwise waves over the simulated actuation range.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated at Re_tau=200 in simulation, so real-world gains may depend on actuation durability, power cost, and scalability to higher Reynolds numbers.
paper_title: Direct numerical simulations of turbulent drag reduction via piezoelectric actuation
